Maladroit

mal-uh-DROYT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Maladroit is unskillful, clumsy, or ineffective.

His maladroit attempt to fix the leaking faucet left the kitchen floor covered in water.

Worked Example

The maladroit apology only made things worse, since the speaker kept accidentally insulting the very people he was trying to comfort.

Maladroit describes a clumsy, poorly handled attempt at something -- physical, social, or verbal -- that ends up making the situation worse rather than better.

How Maladroit Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

clumsy

clumsy: lacking physical or social grace

bungling

bungling: clumsy and ineffective at a task

Antonyms

adroit

adroit: skillful with hands or mind

graceful

graceful: smooth and skillful in execution

How Strong Is It? — awkward → maladroit → hopeless

awkward vs. maladroit

awkward vs. maladroit: An awkward moment might just feel a little clumsy for a second.

hopeless vs. maladroit

hopeless vs. maladroit: A hopeless attempt goes well beyond ordinary clumsiness into total failure.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of maladroit.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — mal-

prefix — mal-: badly (Latin (malus))

root — adroit

root — adroit: skillful (French (a droit, "properly"))

Put it together

Put it together: mal- ("badly") + adroit ("skillful") = badly skillful -- clumsy or ineffective.

Use the root in a new word: malady

Use the root in a new word: malady: The same mal- prefix gives us "malady," a disease or illness you already met as a headword earlier in this course -- literally something that is "badly" with the body.

Root Check

Word Choice

Maladroit is a somewhat formal, literary word -- in casual conversation, 'clumsy' is far more natural, but maladroit fits well in careful writing or a pointed critique.
